description: Labeled end-to-end cases for the Customer Support Resolution Agent capstone (Scenario 1 / Exercise 1). Each case gives the customer message, the model's tool plan (the ordered tool_use/text turns a MockAnthropic router should emit), and the expected outcome the agent must produce. The tests in tests/test_lab22.py assert these outcomes.

model_plan.text: Your order ORD-88213 has shipped; arriving 2026-07-05.

expected.note: The prerequisite gate refuses the order lookup until get_customer verifies identity, preventing action on a misidentified account. Prompt instructions alone have a non-zero failure rate (Sample Question 1).

scenarios.label: $600-refund-blocked-and-escalated
scenarios.message: I need a $600 refund for my damaged order ORD-55100.

model_plan.text: That amount is above my limit, so I've escalated it to a human agent.

expected.note: The interception hook blocks the over-limit refund on every call regardless of the prompt, then builds a structured handoff for the human.

scenarios.label: $400-refund-proceeds
scenarios.message: Please refund $400 for the damage on order ORD-55100.

model_plan.text: Done — I've refunded $400 to your original payment method.

expected.note: $400 is within the $500 ceiling, so the same agent resolves it autonomously — the guardrail blocks only what violates policy.

scenarios.label: explicit-human-request
scenarios.message: This is ridiculous, I want to speak to a human right now.

expected.note: An explicit request for a human is honored immediately, WITHOUT first investigating. Sentiment is not the trigger — the explicit request is.

scenarios.label: multiple-customer-matches->clarify
scenarios.message: Hi, it's Sam Taylor — where's my refund?

model_plan.text: I found more than one account under that name — could you share your customer ID (CUST-...)?

expected.note: Two accounts match the name, so the agent asks for a unique identifier rather than picking one by heuristic. The gate stays locked, so no refund can proceed.

scenarios.label: multi-concern-message
scenarios.message: Where is my order ORD-88213? Also, I need a $40 refund for the damaged charger on order ORD-55100.

model_plan.text: Your order ORD-88213 has shipped (arriving 2026-07-05), and I've refunded $40 for the charger.

expected.note: The message is decomposed into two concerns, each investigated under the shared case context, then synthesized into one unified reply.

model_plan.text: Your order ORD-88213 has shipped and will arrive 2026-07-05.

expected.note: First-contact resolution. Transactional facts (order#, status, amount) are extracted verbatim into the persistent case-facts block, including the $129.99 that came from the tool result rather than the message.
